name: Adani Ports
desc: India's largest private port operator, running Mundra and other ports and terminals plus logistics, rail and marine services.
markets: Ports across India with overseas terminals in Sri Lanka, Israel and elsewhere; customers are shippers and manufacturers.
rationale: Large infrastructure group with international growth plans; F1 offers brand visibility, though B2B marketing is the main use.

name: Celestica
desc: Designs and manufactures hardware for communications, cloud, AI data centre, aerospace and industrial customers as an electronics manufacturing services provider.
markets: Manufacturing sites across North America, Europe and Asia serving hyperscalers, networking firms and aerospace customers.
rationale: B2B technology manufacturer with global footprint; F1 technology showcase could support hyperscaler relationships, but consumer brand needs are low.

name: Cerebras Systems
desc: Makes the Wafer-Scale Engine AI processor and CS-series systems, selling AI hardware and cloud inference services to enterprises and governments.
markets: Customers include enterprises, research labs and sovereign AI buyers in the United States and the Middle East, including G42.
rationale: Fast-growing AI chip brand wanting enterprise visibility; F1 offers technology showcase and hospitality, with AI firms already active in the series.

name: Cloudflare
desc: Provides web infrastructure and security services, including content delivery, DDoS protection, zero-trust security and edge computing for businesses worldwide.
markets: Global network serving customers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions.
rationale: Global enterprise technology brand with a strong network narrative; F1 offers technology showcase and hospitality for enterprise customers.

name: Crusoe
desc: Builds energy-aware AI data centres and offers GPU cloud services, originally using stranded natural gas for computing.
industry: AI data centre and GPU cloud
markets: Data centre campuses in the United States and in Europe serving AI developers and enterprises.
rationale: Fast-growing AI infrastructure brand with energy story; F1 offers technology showcase and B2B hospitality, with AI infrastructure rivals already active.

name: Envision Group
desc: Energy technology group with Envision Energy wind turbines, Envision AESC batteries and green hydrogen and energy storage businesses.
markets: Wind turbine projects and AESC battery plants across Asia, Europe and North America, with automaker customers such as Nissan.
rationale: Global energy brand already in motorsport through its Formula E team, Envision Racing; strong sustainability and technology fit for F1.

name: Equinix
desc: Operates over 250 data centres in about 70 metros, offering colocation, interconnection and digital infrastructure to enterprises and cloud providers.
markets: Data centres across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific serving enterprises and cloud providers.
rationale: Global B2B infrastructure brand with major enterprise customers; F1 offers technology showcase and hospitality for cloud and network clients.

name: Lambda
desc: Offers GPU cloud and AI infrastructure, including NVIDIA GPU clusters, workstations and servers, for AI researchers and enterprises.
markets: Customers are AI researchers, start-ups and enterprises, mainly in the United States; international activity not confirmed.
rationale: AI cloud brand seeking enterprise visibility; F1 offers technology showcase, though footprint and budget are still developing.

name: NEXTDC
desc: Operates data centres in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Canberra, Adelaide and Darwin, offering colocation, interconnection and AI-ready capacity.
markets: Facilities in Australian cities serving enterprises and cloud providers; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Australian B2B infrastructure operator; Australian Grand Prix could provide hospitality for enterprise customers, but its footprint is domestic.

name: Quanta Services
desc: Specialty contractor that designs, builds and maintains power transmission and distribution lines, substations, renewable generation and pipelines.
markets: Operations in the United States, Canada and Australia for utilities and energy customers.
rationale: B2B specialty contractor with little consumer marketing; F1 hospitality could suit utility clients, but fit is limited.

name: Shapoorji Pallonji Group
desc: Indian conglomerate with construction and engineering, real estate, infrastructure, water, energy, shipping and textiles businesses.
markets: Businesses in India with construction projects in the Middle East and Africa; details of current activity not confirmed.
rationale: Large Indian family conglomerate with international projects; F1 hospitality could suit corporate clients, but consumer marketing is limited.

name: Snowflake
desc: Provides a cloud data platform to store, analyse and share data and build AI applications on major clouds.
markets: Enterprise customers across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific, sold on consumption pricing.
rationale: Global enterprise software brand; F1 offers technology showcase and hospitality, with data and cloud software peers already partnered with F1.

name: TeraWulf
desc: Digital infrastructure company that began as a bitcoin miner and is converting sites into high-performance computing and AI data centres.
industry: bitcoin mining and AI data centres
markets: Sites in the United States, including Lake Mariner in New York; no verified international operations.
rationale: Technology-led digital infrastructure firm with limited brand; F1 offers technology showcase in the US, but marketing scale is modest.

name: The Boring Company
desc: Builds underground transport tunnels, including the Las Vegas Convention Center Loop, where Tesla vehicles carry passengers.
markets: Operates loops in Las Vegas, United States, and pursues further US proposals; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Strong media profile and Las Vegas link; Las Vegas Grand Prix offers technology showcase and transport tie-in, though footprint is domestic.

name: WSP Global
desc: Provides engineering design, advisory and project management services for transportation, buildings, water, power and energy projects worldwide.
markets: Offices and projects across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and other regions, serving governments and private clients.
rationale: Global professional services brand; F1 offers hospitality for infrastructure clients and technology showcase, though consumer marketing is limited.

name: CityFibre
desc: UK's largest independent full-fibre network operator, building fibre-to-the-home broadband that is wholesaled to internet providers.
markets: Builds full-fibre networks in UK cities and towns; no international operations.
rationale: UK-only wholesale broadband builder; British Grand Prix could support consumer and partner awareness, but footprint is domestic.

name: Sempra Infrastructure
desc: Develops and operates LNG terminals and natural gas and power infrastructure in the United States and Mexico.
markets: Assets in the United States and Mexico, including LNG export terminals, serving energy customers.
rationale: B2B energy infrastructure arm with limited consumer marketing; F1 races in the US and Mexico offer hospitality but fit is modest.

name: Caterpillar
desc: World's largest maker of construction and mining equipment, engines, turbines and rail products, with financial services under the Cat brand.
markets: Sells machines, engines and services through dealers across North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America.
rationale: Global brand-led industrial company; rivals JCB and Komatsu are already F1 partners, giving a clear technology and hospitality case.

name: Diamond Infrastructure Solutions
desc: Company in Houston, Texas that Crunchbase says focuses on operational infrastructure; its assets and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Texas, United States; assets, customers and international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Little is known about this company, so any F1 fit is speculative and probably weak.

name: EquipmentShare
desc: Rents and sells construction equipment through branches across the United States and offers its T3 telematics and fleet management platform.
markets: Branches across the United States; no verified international operations.
rationale: Fast-growing US equipment brand with technology angle; F1 US races offer hospitality, and peers JCB and Komatsu are partners.

name: Herc Rentals
desc: Rents aerial work platforms, earthmoving equipment, trucks, trailers and specialty tools to construction, industrial and event customers.
markets: Branches in the United States and Canada serving construction, industrial and event customers.
rationale: Equipment rental brand with an events business; US races offer hospitality and event-services visibility, but it has no international ambitions.

name: Taylor Morrison
desc: Designs, builds and sells single-family and multi-family homes in about ten US states under the Taylor Morrison and Esplanade brands.
markets: Communities in US states such as Texas, Florida, Arizona, Colorado and California; no international operations.
rationale: Recognised US consumer home-building brand with no international footprint; F1 fit is limited to US race hospitality.

name: Accelerate
desc: Platform described by Crunchbase as growth-oriented real asset investment, classed under infrastructure and natural resources; its holdings are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Texas, United States; assets, customers and international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Little is known about this investment platform and it has no consumer brand, so F1 fit is very weak.

name: ACCIONA
desc: Spanish group in renewable energy, infrastructure construction, water and services, with wind, solar and hydro power generation and engineering projects.
markets: Projects and energy assets across Europe, the Americas, Africa, the Middle East and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global Spanish brand with a sustainability message; Madrid joins the F1 calendar in 2026, offering strong home-market hospitality and technology showcase.

name: Al Morjan Two Electricity
desc: Special purpose vehicle in Riyadh, classed under construction, apparently formed for a single power project; its owners are not confirmed.
markets: Based in Saudi Arabia; project details, ownership and international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Single-asset vehicle with no brand to market and unclear ownership, so the F1 fit is very weak.
